title: Oriented alteration descent as a special-fibre totalization
statement:
Let $T$ be a Noetherian strictly henselian local scheme with closed point $s$, let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion, and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $T$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-open-immersion]. An ordinary alteration hypercover means an augmented simplicial diagram of Noetherian schemes, finite type over its base, whose maps to matching objects are covers for the Grothendieck topology generated by jointly surjective etale families and proper surjective morphisms [def-weil-pbc-topos, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A matching object is the finite limit prescribed by the faces in the lower simplicial degrees. All these limits and all pullbacks are ordinary scheme-theoretic fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\epsilon:T_\bullet\to T$ be such a hypercover. Set $V_a=V\times_TT_a$, let $j_a:V_a\hookrightarrow T_a$ be the open inclusion, and put $F_a=T_a\times_Ts$ with inclusion $i_a:F_a\hookrightarrow T_a$. On ordinary small etale bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] there is a canonical isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(V,\underline{\mathbf F_\ell})\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{a\geq0}R\Gamma(F_a,i_a^{-1}Rj_{a,*}\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}).$$
Here $R\Gamma$ is derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and $\operatorname{Tot}$ is the derived totalization of the cosimplicial complexes with the alternating sum of coface maps. It admits a functorial first-quadrant double-complex model with total degree equal to simplicial degree plus resolution degree [def-sp-double-complex-total]. The comparison is natural under ordinary Cartesian pullback of the augmented diagram along a local morphism $T'\to T$ between Noetherian strictly henselian local schemes: the induced totalization map is formed from the canonical exchange maps of the $j_a$ and the restriction maps on their special fibres, and agrees with canonical pullback on $R\Gamma(V,-)$. If only degrees $0,\ldots,L$ of a hypercover are specified, with $L\geq1$, the same totalization restricted to those degrees computes $H^q(V,\underline{\mathbf F_\ell})$ for $0\leq q<L$, naturally in such Cartesian pullbacks. No regularity or boundary condition on the $T_a$ is imposed.
